plan_a_advantages: Includes longer, controlled aerobic runs (73 and 63 minutes) which are essential for trail running speed.
Features a dedicated 'aerobic' session, providing a structured opportunity to build endurance beyond just easy running.
Has a more balanced distribution of running volume and intensity.
plan_b_advantages: Prioritizes form work, which is beneficial for efficiency and injury prevention.
Offers a slightly shorter overall training volume (208 minutes vs. 249 minutes).
reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates longer, controlled aerobic runs that are crucial for building the endurance needed for trail racing, alongside shorter, easier runs to maintain consistency. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost entirely on very easy, short trail runs with a strong emphasis on form, which is valuable but insufficient for significant speed development. While form work is important, simply repeating easy runs won't translate to faster times on trails. Plan A’s inclusion of longer runs and a dedicated aerobic session directly addresses the goal of increasing speed and endurance.
